clue.text: She's seen it in one of the tabloids

indicators.note: something seen in a paper sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: 'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A woman spotted in the pages of a red-top newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword convention; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a woman's name, so a female pronoun can stand for her by example.

clue.text: Sea action in which Garibaldi and son may be involved

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so the named letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval action involving the Italian patriot Garibaldi and his son.
explanation.walkthrough: Garibaldi suggests his military campaigns, but his name and 'son' are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsurfing on a board with a sail is an activity carried out on open water, loosely a nautical pursuit.

clue.text: Issue A not quite complete, so is binding B to C?

indicators.note: a word that is not quite complete has lost its final letter
something binding another wraps round it, so these letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: to issue is to emit
A as in one, a single item
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a partly finished edition and how B is bound to C, like a publishing or bookbinding question.
explanation.walkthrough: B and C look like volumes being bound, but they are musical notes: from B up to C is a half-step.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical step from B to C is a half-step, so describing that interval calls for this adjective about half-steps.

clue.text: Half-heartedly swindle peer

indicators.note: half the heart goes, so one of the two central letters is dropped

blocks.note: to nobble is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: A lord tries a half-hearted bit of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBBLE has a double B at its heart; losing one of them, half the heart, leaves NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the aristocracy, a lord or titled aristocrat of rank.

clue.text: "Watch With Mother" interrupts bath-time negotiator

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: lo means look or watch
a familiar word for mother
a quick bath is a dip
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An old BBC children's programme for toddlers breaks into a child's bath-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch With Mother was a BBC television slot for pre-school children; here its words are split up and used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat's job is to negotiate between countries, so a negotiator describes the role.

clue.text: Solemn notes for an extremely unbusy time

blocks.note: first meaning: slow funeral music
second meaning: a month in which nothing at all happens, a lifeless spring month

explanation.surface: Mournful music written to suit a quiet period.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a month that is completely lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral piece played at a slow pace is solemn music; a quiet month is lifeless, or dead.

clue.text: 20ing place making poor rich (but I'll grow to full capacity!)

definitions.note: 20 is STICK: the place where the game of throwing sticks off a bridge began

indicators.note: a letter that grows to its full size is written out as the whole number word
making something out of these letters means building a new arrangement from them

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral written out in full

explanation.surface: A spot that turns paupers into the wealthy, with a playful aside from the letter I.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in POOR RICH becomes ONE, then everything is rearranged. Poohsticks, the bridge game, was invented in The House at Pooh Corner.
explanation.definitionFit: In A. A. Milne's book, Pooh first plays his stick-dropping game near his home, the spot named in the title.

clue.text: Like amnesiacs, left one out, it's clear

indicators.note: letters that are out have been removed from the word

blocks.note: amnesiacs behave forgetfully, unaware of things
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful left something out, which is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L and I from OBLIVIOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'it's clear' before a statement does the same job as the adverb meaning evidently or plainly.

clue.text: One lying ultimately off stage

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one, and off means it is taken away

blocks.note: a, as in one
lying face down

explanation.surface: An actor lies down at last away from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus PRONE without its last letter. 'Off stage' looks like theatre jargon, but 'stage' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a theatre platform projecting in front of the curtain is called by this name.

clue.text: Being urso-microcephalic, 5 shows lexicophobic tendencies

annotation.answer: I AM A BEAR OF VERY LITTLE BRAIN AND LONG WORDS BOTHER ME

blocks.note: surface reading: a scholarly diagnosis full of long Greek and Latin terms
setter's reading: a small-headed bear, and lexicophobic means scared of words, so this is the famous self-description by the bear from 5

explanation.surface: A mock-medical case note about a small-brained bear who fears words.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the clue itself uses exactly the sort of long words that would bother him. 5 refers to Pooh Corner, the bear's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh says this of himself: urso means bear, microcephalic means small-headed, and lexicophobic means afraid of words.

clue.text: So the infernal Guardian heard about man entering claim!

indicators.note: something entering goes inside another, so the person is placed within
about means surrounding, so these letters wrap round all the rest

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
to plead is to claim or allege
a court case that is heard is tried

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a guardian from hell, a man and a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The infernal guardian is Cerberus, the three-headed dog at the gate of Hades; a case a court has heard has been tried.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerberus, the dog guarding the underworld, had three heads, so he is described this way.

clue.text: See 8
See 5
Characters sitting in sauna maturely undressed

definitions.text: Characters sitting in sauna maturely undressed

indicators.note: letters sitting inside a word are its inner ones, without the ends
stripped of its outer covering, a word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: the letters inside this word
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Older people sit naked in a sauna.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: people in a sauna are naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for naked describes sauna users who sit without clothes, as the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Take turns reallocating territory

indicators.note: reallocating hands things out again in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to share land out in rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkestan is a historical region of Central Asia, a broad tract of land rather than one state.

clue.text: See 8
Soapbox that might be taken out by keeper

definitions.text: that might be taken out by keeper

blocks.note: first meaning: a platform for political speeches, as in 'on the campaign trail'

blocks.clueFragment: that might be taken out by keeper
blocks.note: second meaning: one of the three upright posts of a cricket wicket

explanation.surface: A speaker's crate that a goalkeeper or caretaker might remove.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper can knock the bails off and break the wicket; politicians speak 'on the stump' when campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaign speeches are given from a raised platform called this, and a cricket wicket is made of three such posts.

clue.text: One standard we should be proud to raise

definitions.text: One standard we should be proud to raise

blocks.note: a union is a joining into one, a state of oneness
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A patriotic line about a flag the nation should hoist with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a level of quality, but it means a flag; the whole clue also describes the British national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The national flag of the United Kingdom is a banner that British people raise up a pole patriotically.

clue.text: Ornament of gold going about the City

indicators.note: going about something means going round it, so these letters surround the other

blocks.note: French d'or means of gold
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A golden trinket travelling around the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of gold' is translated into French; the City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: The decoration and furnishings of a room are its ornament in the collective sense of adornment.

clue.text: Sweet penchant that made 5 20!

definitions.note: describes something sticky, since 5 is Pooh and 20 is STICK

blocks.note: a sweet food made by bees
a liking, a fondness

explanation.surface: A sweet tooth that got the bear into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh's fondness for honey made him stick in Rabbit's doorway; the answer also describes stickiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling the bee's product is gooey, the quality that left the bear stuck fast.

clue.text: Hut of iron is sent for

indicators.note: of here means made from part of, so the letters come from within the following words

blocks.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A corrugated hut is ordered from the supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hut of iron' reads as one phrase, but 'Hut' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen is a prefabricated corrugated-steel shelter with a half-cylinder roof, used by the military.

clue.text: What moves me? It's water under the bridge for 5 and co

definitions.text: What moves me? It's water under the bridge for 5 and co

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for something past and forgotten
setter's reading: the item dropped off a bridge in Pooh's game is carried along by the stream below

explanation.walkthrough: 5 is Pooh Corner, so '5 and co' are Pooh and friends, who drop twigs from a bridge and watch which floats out first.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poohsticks each player drops a twig into the river and the current carries it under the bridge.

clue.text: Twice one becomes free - little change here

indicators.note: one thing becomes another when it is swapped for it

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
open, as in free to all

explanation.surface: Doubling one makes something free, which is a small change.
explanation.walkthrough: In TWICE the I is replaced by OPEN. Twopence was a small British coin value, two pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pennies is a tiny sum of coins, so the answer is a small amount of loose money.

clue.text: A private lubrication to rub in up the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way up a down entry, the letters run backwards
rubbing something in works it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: oil lubricates
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldier's slang about applying grease against the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A private' is the definition, not a description of the lubrication: a poilu was a French infantryman of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for a French ordinary soldier of the Great War, so a private of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Great Olympian raising the course of the water

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising lifts the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: the Suez Canal is a famous man-made waterway

explanation.surface: A mighty god lifts a river's course.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of the gods lived on Mount Olympus, the greatest of its divine residents.

clue.text: See 8
Not moving cattle in the way things are

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the state of not moving

indicators.note: in places the animals inside the other phrase

blocks.note: kine is an old plural of cow
as is: in the present condition

explanation.surface: Livestock standing still, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: KINE goes inside AS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for loss or absence of muscular movement, so a state of stillness.

clue.text: Being in bed topless is strange in the North

indicators.note: with its top removed, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: bunked down, slept in a bunk

explanation.surface: Lying in bed half-naked is odd up north.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNKED loses its first letter. Unked is a dialect word from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This regional dialect word means odd, uncanny or awkward, used in northern counties of England.
